appraisal_events.evidence: Vous avez le flair le plus fin de toutes ces choses-là et je ne veux pas avoir l'air de quémander des invités. En tout cas, sur vous, je compte absolument.
appraisal_events.explanation: Immediately after being snubbed by Charlus, Mme de Saint-Euverte turns to the narrator, praises his social tact, and declares she is relying entirely on him to mediate, admitting him into her confidence.

appraisal_events.evidence: je ne le raconterai qu'à une seule personne, et cette personne, cela va être vous.
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann singles out the narrator as the one person to whom he will confide his exchange with the Prince, marking him as uniquely trusted.

status_effects.explanation: Both Mme de Saint-Euverte and Swann single the narrator out for special trust and confidence in this stretch, marginally elevating his social inclusion as a valued intermediary and confidant.

ambiguities: Swann dismisses as entirely invented and stupid a rumor about his exchange with the Prince, which the narrator earlier attributed to marquis de Bréauté but withheld from Swann; this plausibly discredits Bréauté by association, but since Swann never learns or names the source within the scene, this was judged too indirect to score as a distinct event for Bréauté.
